text:
Maya: Quick Q — where are the go-to dashboards for GPU SM% + KV cache hit across prod clusters? Need to tune alerts before the canary tomorrow.

Tom: Grafana -> \"GPU / Serving / Cluster Overview\" has SM% heatmaps and per-GPU mem. KV cache panels are in \"Serving / KV Cache\" (hitrate, evictions). Links: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/gpu-cluster, https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/kv-cache

Maya: thanks — do we have a prom query for 5m avg SM% I can paste into a ticket?

Tom: yup, use this for avg SM across GPUs: ```avg(avg_over_time(gpu_sm_utilization[5m])) by (cluster)``` For per-GPU: ```avg_over_time(gpu_sm_utilization[5m]) by (gpu_id)```

Kai: FYI traces for weird spikes live in Tempo — if you have a trace id from the dash click the orange trace icon. Or search service=serving-engine and tag cluster. Tempo link: https://tempo.redwood.ai/search

Ashley: Alert tuning context: current high-SM alert fires at >96% for 3m (alerts/HighGpuSM). We were getting noisy on backfills; suggestion: raise to 98% or add `for: 5m` and scope to p99 sessions. For KV cache low-hitrate alerts it's currently <60% for 10m. If your workload is bursty, consider >50% with a mute during nightly evals.

Maya: Can you paste a quick example of the alert rule change for Prometheus?

Ashley: sure — example snippet: ```groups:
- name: serving.rules
  rules:
  - alert: HighGpuSM
    expr: avg_over_time(gpu_sm_utilization[5m]) > 0.98
    for: 5m
    labels:
      severity: page
    annotations:
      summary: "High GPU SM% on {{ $labels.cluster }}"
  - alert: LowKvHitrate
    expr: avg_over_time(kv_cache_hitrate[10m]) < 0.5
    for: 10m
    labels:
      severity: warning
    annotations:
      summary: "Low KV cache hitrate on {{ $labels.cluster }}"```

Tom: small note — metric names are `gpu_sm_utilization` (0-1) and `kv_cache_hitrate` (0-1). In dashboards we show % but alerts use fractional values.

Maya: perfect. Also where do I find the GPU memory per process? Need to know which tasks hog mem.

Tom: check node exporter + serving process metrics: `process_resident_memory_bytes{job="serving"}` or Grafana panel \"Serving / Process memory by PID\". If you need a one-off: use `top` on the VM or `nvidia-smi pmon -c 1`.

Maya: great — I'll open a PR to bump HighGpuSM to 98% and add a silence during the canary. Ping me for review if you have bandwidth @Tom @Ashley :thumbsup:

Tom: ack, will review later today.

Kai: lmk if you want me to attach trace examples to the PR. I can pull a couple from last week.

Maya: please do — attaching traces will help justify the thresholds. Thanks everyone! :pray:
